speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and dysuria. To begin our assessment, can you tell me exactly where in your abdomen the pain is located and if you have experienced any fever or changes in your urine color?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old female. The patient presents with a 5-day history of severe abdominal pain and cramping, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. She reports pain with urination and also experienced burning pain during sexual intercourse 3 days ago. She mentions being sexually active with one male partner, using condoms inconsistently.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID) secondary to an STI. The combination of dysuria, severe abdominal pain, vomiting, and dyspareunia in a sexually active 17-year-old is highly suggestive of PID, likely caused by Chlamydia or Gonorrhea ascending from the lower urinary tract. I recommend immediate treatment and further testing.
